la:verb:obtempero.gloss: to comply with; to conform to, obey
senses: to comply with; to conform to, obey
la:verb:obtempero.html:
ob-tempĕro (opt-), āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to comply with, attend to, conform to, submit to, obey (cf.: oboedio, obsequor, pareo; class.).
With dat.: te audi, tibi obtempera,: alicui obtemperare et parere,: imperio populi Romani,: voluntati alicujus,: auctoritati senatūs,; : rationi obtemperare debet gubernator, Müll.: naturae,: qui obtemperet ipse sibi, et decretis suis pareat,who conforms to his own precepts,: tibi deos certo scio obtemperaturos magis,they will regard you,.—
With ad: ad id, quod ex verbis intellegi possit, obtemperare,.—
With rel.-clause (perh. only in Plaut.): non ego illi obtempero quod loquitur,do not mind what he says,: quae dico,. —
Impers. pass.: quominus eis optemperetur, Lex. Jul. Municip. fin. ap. Haub. p. 133: si mihi esset obtemperatum,.—Hence, obtempĕranter, adv., willingly, readily, obediently (postAug.): se obtemperanter nobis accommodat, M. Aurel. ap. Mai.: annuit, Prud. στεφ. 2, 112.

la:verb:obturbo.gloss: to stir up, disturb, make turbid
senses: to stir up, disturb, make turbid
la:verb:obturbo.html:
ob-turbo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to stir up, make turbid.
Lit.: obturbata proculcatione prius aqua,. —
Trop., to throw into disorder or confusion; to disorder, confuse, trouble, disturb, distract: (eos) denso agmine obturbabat,: ne obturba, ac tace,: lectorem,; cf.: obturbatur militum vocibus,: me scriptio et litterae non leniunt sed obturbant,distract,: solitudinem,to disturb,.— Absol.: obturbabant patres specie detestandi, to raise a disturbance or clamor, (30 Ritter).—Impers.: obturbatur, obstrepitur,.

la:verb:obtineo.gloss: to have, occupy, possess, hold, obtain
senses: to have, occupy, possess, hold, obtain
to preserve, keep, maintain, uphold; persist in
to assert, show, prove, demonstrate, maintain
to gain, acquire, obtain, achieve, win
to maintain oneself, prevail, succeed, last, stand, continue
la:verb:obtineo.html:
ob-tĭnĕo (opt-), tĭnŭi, tentum, 2 (old
perf. OPTENVI, fifth Epit. of the Scipios; inf. pass. obtinerier, ; ), v. a. and n.
teneo
.
Act. *
To take hold of, hold: obtine aures, amabo,.—
To hold, have, occupy, possess; to preserve, keep, maintain, etc. (class.).
In gen.: sancte Apollo, qui umbilicum certum terrarum obtines, Poët. ap. (Trag. Rel. p. 201 Rib.): suam quisque domum tum obtinebat,: armis Galliam atque Italiam,: cum imperio Hispaniam citeriorem,to have as his province, to be governor in it,: Galliam et Italiam,: Africam,; cf.: ex quā insulā nummus nullus, me obtinente, erogabitur,during my administration,: QVEI AERARIVM PROVINCIAM OBTINEBIT, who will have the administration of the public treasure, Lex Thor. § 20 Rudorff. p. 168; Lex de Scribis ap. Haubold, p. 85: necessitudinem cum publicanis,: vitam et famam,to preserve,: auctoritatem suam,to maintain,: principatum,: regnum,: jus,to assert, maintain,: causam,: noctem insequentem eadem caligo obtinuit,occupied, took up, prevailed during,: quae (fama) plerosque obtinet,: proverbii locum obtinet,i. e. is become proverbial,: parentis gravitatem,: numerum deorum,to be numbered among,; so, aliquem numerum,; cf. : summam opinionem

m scholis, : admirationem,to be admired,: patriae nomen,: firmitudinem animi,i. e. exhibited,: pontem,would not yield,: silentiam,to maintain,.—With inf., to persist in: earumque artem et disciplinam obtineat colere,.—

In partic., of speech, to assert, maintain, i. e. to show, prove, demonstrate: possumus hoc teste ... quod dicimus, obtinere?: duas contrarias sententias,: diu pugnare in iis, quae obtinere non possis,: recta apud turpes,: quaedam (leges) an obtineri possint,; : quod orator praecipue sibi obtinendum intellegit, Spald. N. cr. (al. proponendum); cf. : si defecerint omnia, tum videndum erit, an obtineri possit, ne illud quidem recte factum,; .—
To get possession of; to gain, acquire, obtain something (syn.: assequor, adipiscor, impetro; class.): quanta instrumenta habeat (homo) ad obtinendam adipiscendamque sapientiam,: impetrare et obtinere,; : malas causas semper obtinuit, in optimā concidit,gained,; cf. : jus suum contra aliquem,: Romani si rem obtinuerint,if they gained the victory,: voluimus quaedam; obtenta non sunt,: apud eum causam obtinuit,: aditu regis obtento,.—Hence, to conquer, overcome (eccl. Lat.): melius est ut pugnemus contra eos in campestribus, et obtinebimus eos,; 20, 25; id. Judith, 1, 5.—
Neutr. (cf. teneo, II.), to maintain itself; to hold, prevail, last, stand, continue, obtain (not in Cic.): quod et plures tradidere auctores et fama obtinuit,; cf. with a subject-clause: pro vero antea obtinebat, regna atque imperia Fortunam dono dare, Sall. Rep. Ordin. init.: non ipsos quoque fuisse pastores obtinebit, quod? etc.,: si dissentirent, sententia plurium obtineret,would prevail,: quod merito obtinuit,.—Absol.: obtinuit (sc. consuetudo),.—With de: quia de intercalando non obtinuerat, Cael. ap. .—With ut or ne: his obtinuit, ut praeferretur candidato,; : obtinuit, ne reus fieret,.—With quin, .

la:noun:obtrectatio.html:
obtrectātĭo, ōnis, f.
obtrecto
,
an envious detracting, disparaging; detraction, disparagement (class.): obtrectatio est ea, quam intellegi ζηλοτυπίαν volo, aegritudo ex eo, quod alter quoque potiatur eo, quod ipse concupiverit, : invidia atque obtrectatio,; cf. Orell. N. cr.; : et malevolentia,: et invidentia,: et livor,: malevolentissimae,; cf.: malevolorum obtrectationes et invidias prosternere, Vat. ap. : adversus gloriam,.—
With gen. obj.: laudis,: gloriae alienae,.

la:noun:obtrectator.html:
obtrectātor, ōris, m.
id.
,
a detractor, traducer, disparager (class.): obtrectator est, qui facit quid contra recte tractantem, Paul. ex Müll.: beneficii,: multi communes obtrectatores atque omnium invidi, multa finxerunt,: obtrectatores et invidi Scipionis,; : non relinquere locum obtrectatorum sermoni,: contra inimicos atque obtrectatores,: laudum mearum,.—
With dat.: huic sententiae obtrectatores amici regis erant,.

la:verb:obtestor.gloss: to call someone as a witness
senses: to call someone as a witness
to beseech or implore, to beg
la:verb:obtestor.html:
ob-testor, ātus, 1, v. dep.,
to call as a witness to any thing; to protest or assert by a person or thing (syn.: testor, obsecro, supplico; class.).
In gen.: necessitudinem nostram tuamque in me benevolentiam obtestans,: deūm hominumque fidem,: sacra regni, deos et hospitales mensas,: summam rempublicam agi obtestans,: aut militum se manibus aut suis moriturum obtestans,; —
Transf., to conjure by calling to witness; to entreat, beseech, supplicate, implore: per ego haec genua te,; : per omnes deos te obtestor, ut, etc.,; : vos judices,: vos obtestor atque obsecro, ut, etc.,: id sibi ne eripiatis, vos obtestatur,: obsistens obtestansque deum et hominum fidem testabatur, nequiquam eos fugere,. —With double acc.: illud te ... Pro Latio obtestor, ne, etc.,.—Part.: obtestātus, a, um, in the pass. signif., earnestly entreated, supplicated, implored: obtestatus prece impensā,: obtestatā fide,.

la:verb:obtendo.gloss: to stretch or spread before or over
senses: to stretch or spread before or over
la:verb:obtendo.html:
ob-tendo, di, tum, 3, v. a.
To draw, stretch, spread, or place before (cf. obtego; not freq. till after the Aug. per.).
Lit.
Proque viro nebulam et ventos obtendere inanes, : sudarium ante faciem,.—Poet.: obtentā nocte,i. e. in dark night,.—
Pass., with mid. force: oculis membrana obtenditur,spreads over,: Britannia Germaniae obtenditur,lies over against Germany,.—
Trop., to pretend, allege, plead as an excuse: matris preces obtendens,: ad ea Drusus cum arbitrium senatūs obtenderet,: valetudinem corporis, aetatem liberūm, nubilem filiam,: suae imbecillitati sanitatis appellationem obtendunt,: rationem turpitudini, : qui delictis suis excusationem carnis obtendet,: quid poterimus obtendere,plead what excuse,.—
Transf., to cover, hide, conceal.
Lit.: obtendunt limina silvis,: lucem pulvere,: diem nube atrā,.—
Trop., to hide, conceal, envelop: quasi velis quibusdam obtenditur uniuscujusque natura,.—
To spread over, make a cover for: Vitellius curis luxum obtendebat,i. e. sought a refuge from,

la:noun:obtutus.gloss: an instance of seeing or looking at, a gaze
senses: an instance of seeing or looking at, a gaze
la:noun:obtutus.html:
obtūtus, ūs, m.
obtueor
,
a seeing, looking at or upon any thing (class., but in prose always with oculorum, unless this word is obviously supplied by the context; cf. aspectus): obtutu quasi obtuitu a verbo tuor quod significat video, Paul. ex Müll.: oculorum,; so ; : obtutum aliquo figere, id. poët. N. D. 2, 42, 107: dum stupet, obtutuque haeret defixus in uno,: obtutu tacito stetit,: defixa Latinus Obtutu tenet ora,: oculi in uno obtutu defixi, Sen. de Ira, 3, 4 init.—Trop.: in obtutu malorum,in the contemplation of,.—In plur.: nil intecurrens obtutibus,.—
(Late Lat.) The eye: quis ita gemino obtutu eluminatus. .—More freq. in plur.: ita videri nostris obtutibus constitutis,; : humi prostrati sub obtutibus ejus,.

la:verb:obtectus.html:
obtectus, ūs, m.
obtego
,
a covering (late Lat.), Jul. ap. Aug. c. Sec. Resp. Jul. 4, 65.

la:verb:obtrunco.html:
ob-trunco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to cut off, lop away; to trim, prune.
Lit. (post-Aug. and very rare): vitem,.—
In gen., to cut down, cut to pieces, kill, slay, slaughter (not in Cic. or Cæs.; syn.: trucido, jugulo, occido): ipsus Amphitruo optruncavit regem Pterelam in proelio,: (Medea) puerum interea obtruncat, Poët. ap. : ceteri vice pecorum obtruncabantur, ap. : caedere alios, alios obtruncare,: regem,: (hostes),: cervos ferro,: gallum,; ; ; ; ; ; ; .

la:noun:obtentus.html:
ob-tentus (opt-), ūs, m.
obtendo
.
A drawing, spreading, or placing before (poet. and post-Aug.).
Lit.: obtentu togae, tamquam se amiciens, ne videretur,: frondis,: nubium,.—
Trop., a pretence, pretext, color (cf.: simulatio, species): obtentum habere,: tempora reipublicae obtentui sumpta,assumed as a pretext,: sub obtentu liberationis,: damnationis,: sub obtentu monituum deorum quaedam enuntiare, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 3, 6.—
(Acc. to obtendo, II.) A covering, cover, veil (post-class.): quia secundae res mire sunt vitiis optentui,: vera sunt, quae loquuntur poëtae, sed obtentu aliquo specieque velata,disguise, allegorical dress,: non terror obtentui est,a hinderance,.

la:verb:obtexo.html:
ob-texo, xŭi, 3, v. a. (post-Aug.).
To weave to or over any thing: papilio fila araneosa alarum lanugine obtexit,.—
To weave over, i. e. to overspread, cover with any thing: caelum obtexitur umbrā,: per nubes caelum aliud obtexens,: jaculis obtexitur aër,.—Transf.: excusationes obtexere avaritiae suae,: sol nubibus obtexitur,.

la:verb:obtego.html:
ob-tĕgo (collat. form obtĭgo, ), xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to cover over, cover up (for protection or concealment) (syn.: obtendo, velo, celo; class.).
Lit.: insuper lingua bubula obtegito,: in pectus perpluit meum, neque jam umquam obtigere possum,: domus arboribus obtecta,: armis,: se servorum et libertorum corporibus,: os obtegendum, fauces velandae,. —
Trop., to veil, hide, conceal, keep secret: obtegere errata,: vitia multis virtutibus obtecta,: ut adulescentiae turpitudo obscuritate obtegatur,: nihil,: scelera nuper reperta priscis verbis,: flagitia,.— With gen.: animus audax, sui obtegens in alios criminator,.—
To protect: aegre precibus meliorum obtectus,.

la:verb:obtundo#2.html:
ob-tundo, tŭdi, tūsum (and tunsum), 3, v. a.
To strike or beat against, at, or on a thing; to beat, thump, belabor (very rare; perh. only ante- and post-class.): pectora pugnis, Firm. Math. 5, 5: obtundit os mihi,breaks my jaw,; cf.: obtunso ore,; cf.: nam sum obtusus pugnis pessume,.—
To blunt, dull, by striking.
Lit. (very rare): telum,: gladios,.—
Transf.
To blunt, weaken, make dull, deprive of strength: aciem oculorum,: auditum,: obtusus stomachus,: vocem,to blunt, weaken,: ingenia,: et obtusis ceciderunt viribus artis,; : mentem,: ingenia,: nihil est quod tam obtundat elevetque aegritudinem, quam. etc.,.—
Aures or aliquem, or simply obtundere, to stun or din the ears; to deafen one by saying a thing too often or too long; hence, to annoy or tease with importunity; aures graviter obtundo tuas, ne quem ames, : ne brevitas

defraudasse aures videatur, neve longitudo obtudisse, : aliquem longis epistulis,to annoy, molest,: aliquem,: rogitando,.—With object-clause: obtuderunt ejus aures, te socium praetoris fuisse, they dinned into him that, etc., Timarch. ap. .— With subj.: non cessat obtundere, totam prorsus a principio fabulam promeret,: aliquem de aliquā re,to importune, annoy,: obtundis, tametsi intellego, etc.,.—Hence, obtūsus (obtunsus or optūsus), a, um, P. a., blunt, dull, obtuse (class.).

Lit.: falx obtusa et hebes,: pugio,: vomer,: angulus,: cornua lunae obtusa,.—
Transf., blunted, blunt, dull, weak, faint, powerless: animi acies obtusior,: stellis acies obtunsa,: obtusi et hebetes ad aliquam rem, ap. : aures obtunsae,blunted, dull of hearing,: vox, thick, not clear (opp. clara), : fauces tumentes strangulant vocem, optusae obscurant,: stomachus,weakened, spoiled,: obtunsa pectora,insensible, without feeling,: ingenium,: vires,enfeebled,: nimio ne luxu obtunsior usus Sit genitali arvo,too blunted, too enfeebled,: vigor animi,: cor,: sensus eorum,: venenum,powerless,.—Comp.: quo quid dici potest obtusius?.—Sup. does not occur.—Hence, adv.: obtūsē, dully, not keenly (postclass.): crocodili in aquā obtusius vident, in terrā acutissime,.—Fig.: hoc facere obtuse,.

obtentus, a, um.
Part., from obtendo.—
Part., from obtineo.

la:verb:obtero.gloss: to bruise, crush or break to pieces
senses: to bruise, crush or break to pieces
to degrade, disgrace, contemn, disparage, ravage, destroy
la:verb:obtero.html:
ob-tĕro (opt-), trīvi, trītum, 3 (
pluperf. subj. obtrisset for obtrivisset, Drak. N. cr.; perf. obterii, ), v. a.
To bruise, crush, or break to pieces (syn. obtundo; class.).—Lit.: ne in stabulo infantes grex boum obtereret,: ranas,: puerum,: homines,: caput saxo,: locustarum ova,: crura,: in angustiis portarum obtriti sunt,crushed by the crowd,.—
Trop., to crush, trample on, degrade, disgrace, contemn, disparage, ravage, destroy: meaeque pugnae proeliares plurumae optritae jacent?: calumniam,: laudem imperatoriam,: obtrectationes,: jura populi,: legionarios,: Graeciam,: militem verbis,to degrade,: Penates,: vulgi omne cadaver,.—*
To rub: dentes carbone,.

la:verb:obturo.html:
obtūro, āvi, ātum, 1 (old
inf. pass. obturarier, ), v. a., to stop up, to close (class.; syn.: oblino, obstruo).
Lit.: gutturem,: os,: foramina,: dolia operculis,: aures,i. e. to refuse to listen,; obstructas eas partes et obturatas esse,: oculos,: ora leonum,.—
Trop., to assuage, allay: amorem edendi,.

la:verb:obticesco.html:
obtĭcesco (opt-), tĭcŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. [obticeo], to become or be struck silent; in perf., to be silent (syn. obmutesco): obticuit obticescit,: quid, amabo, opticuisti?: quid nunc obticuisti? (dub.; Umpfenb. and Fleck. obstipuisti): repente obticuit,: nec prius obticuit quam, etc.,: chorus,; .—With acc.: cetera obticuit, Lact. Ira Dei, 4, 13.

la:verb:obtingo.html:
ob-tingo (opt-), tĭgi, 3, v. a. and n.
tango
. *
Act., to touch, strike: mustulentus aestus nares obtigit, Plaut. Fragm. ap. . (The same fragm., , has attigit.)—
Neutr., to fall to one's lot (syn.: accidit, evenit, contingit): naufragio res contigit. Nempe ergo haud Fortuna obtigit, Pac. ap. : nullus est, quoi non invideant rem secundam obtingere,: dies mihi adversus,: mihi propter te hoc optigit,: quod cuique obtigit, id quisque teneat,: mihi obtinget sors,; cf.: cum tibi aquaria provincia sorte obtigisset,: cum optatissimum nuntium accepissem, te mihi quaestorem obtigisse,; : quam mihi obtigisse dicis σπἀρταν, numquam deseram, : omnia, quae hominibus forte obtigerunt,: quae (vox, latus, etc.) si modica obtigerunt, possunt ratione ampliari, id. praef. § 27.—With ut: cum ei (L. Paulo), bellum ut cum rege Perse gereret, obtigisset,it had fallen to his lot,.—
Of events, to happen, befall, occur (in this sense accidere, contingere, evenire, etc., are more common): eloquere, ut haec res obtigit de filiā, has happened, taken place, turned out: id quom optigerat,; : istuc tibi ex sententiā tuā obtigisse, laetor,: hoc confiteor jure Mi obtigisse,: praeter spem,: si quid obtigerit, aequo animo paratoque moriar,if any thing should happen to me,—In plur.: exoptata obtingent,.

la:noun:obtemperatio.html:
obtempĕrātĭo, ōnis, f.
obtempero
,
a complying with or submitting to; compliance, submission, obedience; with dat.: si justitia est obtemperatio scriptis legibus,.

,

Bluntness, dulness (eccl. Lat.): obtusio sensuum,; : visus,.— Absol., ; .

la:verb:obtrecto.html:
ob-trecto, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
[tracto], to detract from through envy; to disparage, underrate, decry; to be opposed to; to thwart; to injure a person or thing (class.; syn. detrecto; cf.: aemulo, invideo); constr. with dat. or acc.
With dat.: obtrectare alicui,; cf. : bonis,: gloriae alicujus,; : laudibus ducis,: legi, atque causae,.—
With acc. (so perh. not ante-Aug.): sin livor obtrectare curam voluerit,to detract from, carp at, epil. 10: laudes alicujus,: urbanas excubias,: se invicem, .—
With inter se, to be rivals: obtrectārunt inter se,. —
Absol.: obtrectantis est angi alieno bono,: obtrectandi causā,: ne aut obstare aut obtrectare praesens videretur,.

Transf., blunted, blunt, dull, weak, faint, powerless: animi acies obtusior,: stellis acies obtunsa,: obtusi et hebetes ad aliquam rem, ap. : aures obtunsae,blunted, dull of hearing,: vox, thick, not clear (opp. clara), : fauces tumentes strangulant vocem, optusae obscurant,: stomachus,weakened, spoiled,: obtunsa pectora,insensible, without feeling,: ingenium,: vires,enfeebled,: nimio ne luxu obtunsior usus Sit genitali arvo,too blunted, too enfeebled,: vigor animi,: cor,: sensus eorum,: venenum,powerless,.—Comp.: quo quid dici potest obtusius?.—Sup. does not occur.—Hence, adv.: obtūsē, dully, not keenly (postclass.): crocodili in aquā obtusius vident, in terrā acutissime,.—Fig.: hoc facere obtuse,.
